scores.notes: Worshippers entering at the temple gate are present at 3:2; their wonder anticipates 3:10 but adds no named or recurring figure.
Both name the same flaw: 'waiting lobsters and turtles on the shingle' come from the song, not the scene ('We can do without lobsters'). It is an added figure, not a speaker drawn inside the words.
A law verse whose content is the pig; the plan puts its recipients Moses and Aaron in as the subject, 'teaching the people'.
'Israelites distant on the far shore' and Moses on the bank conflict with Israel 'in the middle of the sea' (14:22-23).
Hezekiah's copyists, who transmit the proverb, are drawn into it (one fault, the writer inside the words); 'pause mid-copying' asks for writing in progress.
The letter's writer Paul is seated among its Corinthian readers acting out 'face to face'.
'Faint shapes of the redeemed' are unnamed and incidental; the plan's flaw is New Jerusalem descending, the next verse, already marked as the wrong moment.
Martha is at the tomb in the section (11:39-40); Lazarus stirring inside at the cry is the same instant, not his coming out.
God is not in the section cast and is never drawn; the flaw is the speaker Isaiah acting in God's place, already marked.
'Scattered loose newspapers litter the seats' asks for open print and contradicts 'rolled them all into a gigantic ball'.
A 'radiant cloud ... suggesting Yahweh's gaze' puts a divine presence in the hall that the seer only speaks of; God is not in this section's cast.
Jesse and David are names in a genealogy, not people this verse shows in a scene; the plan's flaw is the earlier nursing scene, already marked as the wrong moment.
